findings.title: traceID field dropped from Plugin Request Completed log line
findings.body: The old LoggerMiddleware.logRequest explicitly retrieved the trace ID via tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false) and appended it to the log params when non-empty. The new implementation calls m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...) with no equivalent step, and the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware (which now owns the contextual attribute injection) only adds endpoint/pluginId/dsName/dsUID/uname — it never adds traceID. As a result the "Plugin Request Completed" log line loses the traceID key that operators previously relied on to correlate plugin request logs with distributed traces. The traceID is still attached as a Prometheus exemplar in MetricsMiddleware, so the value is available in metrics, but it is no longer present in the request log.

findings.title: New ContextualLoggerMiddleware has no test file
findings.body: The PR adds a brand-new middleware (NewContextualLoggerMiddleware / ContextualLoggerMiddleware) that is now responsible for enriching the request context with endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID, and uname, and the LoggerMiddleware was changed to depend on that enrichment. Despite this, no contextual_logger_middleware_test.go is added. The existing tests only cover the renamed MetricsMiddleware. Without a test that exercises the four endpoints (QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth, CollectMetrics) and verifies the contextual attributes are attached to the context, regressions in the enrichment logic (e.g. wrong field names, missing nil checks, or an endpoint that forgets to call instrumentContext) will not be caught.

findings.title: LoggerMiddleware silently loses fields when ContextualLoggerMiddleware is absent
findings.body: logRequest was changed from m.logger.Info(...) (self-contained: it explicitly appended pluginId, endpoint, uname, dsName, dsUID, traceID) to m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...). The contextual attributes now come exclusively from ContextualLoggerMiddleware, which sits directly above LoggerMiddleware in CreateMiddlewares. If anyone reorders, removes, or conditionally skips ContextualLoggerMiddleware (the middleware is newly added and easy to miss), the "Plugin Request Completed" log line will lose endpoint, pluginId, uname, dsName, dsUID with no warning. The previous code was self-sufficient; the new code has a hidden ordering dependency. This should at minimum be documented on the function/middleware, or the fields should be re-added as fallbacks.

findings.title: FromContext doc comment is incorrect
findings.body: The comment "FromContext returns a new contextual Logger that has this logger's context plus the given context" implies FromContext merges additional context into the receiver, but the implementation (grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext in logger.go) actually extracts a *log.ConcreteLogger that was previously stored in ctx (via log.WithContextualAttributes) and rewraps it. The new logger is not "this logger's context plus the given context" — it is whatever the context already carries. The comment should describe that FromContext returns a Logger populated with the contextual attributes already present in ctx (returning a fresh logger if none are found). The same wording was previously used for New, where it is also inaccurate because New takes variadic any key/value pairs, not a context.

findings.title: New doc comment misdescribes the parameter
findings.body: The comment "New returns a new contextual Logger that has this logger's context plus the given context" was left unchanged, but New takes ctx ...any (key/value pairs) — not a context.Context. Combined with the newly added FromContext that does take a context.Context, the two methods are easy to confuse. The comment should be updated to describe New as taking key/value context attributes (e.g. "New returns a new contextual Logger that has this logger's context plus the given key/value pairs").

findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext ignores its argument
findings.body: TestLogger.FromContext(_ context.Context) Logger discards the context and returns a brand-new TestLogger, so any test that uses TestLogger to exercise code paths which now go through FromContext (notably the rewritten LoggerMiddleware.logRequest, which calls m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)) cannot assert that the contextual attributes placed in ctx by ContextualLoggerMiddleware actually reach the log call. The fake should at minimum capture the supplied context (or the contextual attributes derived from it) so tests can verify the propagation; otherwise the new dependency between LoggerMiddleware and ContextualLoggerMiddleware is untestable through this fake.

findings.title: instrumentContext name is a leftover from the old InstrumentationMiddleware
findings.body: The function is named instrumentContext, but it lives in ContextualLoggerMiddleware and only adds log key/value pairs to the context — it does no instrumentation in the metrics/tracing sense. The name was carried over verbatim from the old InstrumentationMiddleware. Renaming to e.g. addContextualAttributes or withPluginContextLogAttrs would make the new file self-describing.
